lead_headline: Douglas County foreclosure hits $6.1M while restaurant openings pause — zero new leads tracked today

restaurant.blurb: Zero new leads today for second consecutive day holds pipeline at 119 (62 openings, 57 closures). Recent activity: The Flaming Grill (CBD Indian fusion), Olive & Finch (Golden Triangle expansion).

foreclosure.blurb: $6.14M Douglas County filing at 18901 Longs Way leads this week's activity — the only notice exceeding $4M threshold among 74 total filings.

liquor.blurb: Zero new applications today extends Thursday's traditional filing lull as operators await weekend. The 7-day total holds at 16 applications, matching last week's volume exactly — a rare week-over-week flat performance suggesting licensing velocity has stabilized after March's volatility. Recent activity included restaurant-heavy Wednesday filings (The Pit Shop, El Pulgarcito de Bukele, Culture) before Thursday-Friday's predictable dropoff.

reputation.blurb: 6 mentions yesterday (Instagram 4, Denver Post 1, Facebook 1) lifts 7-day total to 46 across 9 sources — down 12% from last week's 52 but reversing three consecutive weekly declines. Instagram (13) reclaims weekly dominance ahead of Denver Post/Facebook/X.com (6 each) and Hoodline (5). Yesterday's bounce driven by Green Collective rebrand coverage (Denver Post), Red Rocks merchandise promotion (Instagram), and downtown development speculation. The stabilization at 46 weekly mentions suggests media interest has bottomed after April's sharp descent from March highs.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) marks sixth consecutive zero-change day, holding MTD at +18 (+0.8/day) and 90-day net at +141. This week delivered just +3 net (4 new, 1 canceled) — a 73% collapse from last week's +11 performance as late-April momentum evaporates. The extended flatline contrasts sharply with early April's front-loaded conversion: the first 11 days generated +16 net before momentum stalled mid-month. YTD's +1.3/day pace continues outpacing MTD's anemic +0.8/day rate, reflecting stronger Q1 fundamentals that have yet to carry into April's final week.
